questions.key_step: King property $x\to\pi-x$ gives $f=\pi\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{1-\cos^2t\sin^2x}=\frac{\pi^2}{\sin t}$.
questions.justification: Three linked stages (king property, parametric standard integral via $\tan x$, outer integral) with a numerical answer and a parameter $t$ to track; each stage is a known pattern.

questions.key_step: Recognise the Riemann sum, divide by $x^2$ and put $t=x+\frac{1}{x}$ to get $\int\frac{dt}{t\sqrt{t^2-2}}$.
questions.justification: Chain: infer the general term from a partly written sum, Riemann-sum conversion, the less common $x+\frac{1}{x}$ substitution, then a second substitution and arctangent; numerical answer with no options, so one slip fails.
